verdicts.summary: A biomarker with a clean epithelial signal, but no functional study in either direction, so the 'validated target' claim is unearned.

reasons.text: Reproducible, intrinsic, epithelial rise and a secreted protein make a tractable test, but the card itself shows no functional study; its role could be repair, so inhibition may harm.

verdicts.summary: An existing MD-2 antagonist makes a cheap test, but the neutrophil-driven signal and a healing penalty from TLR4/MD-2 blockade call for caution.

reasons.text: Antibody blockade of TLR4/MD-2 lowered inflammation in DSS colitis but impaired mucosal healing during recovery.
reasons.quote: Our findings suggest that anti-TLR4 therapy may decrease inflammation in IBD but may also interfere with colonic mucosal healing.

reasons.text: Much of the bulk rise is neutrophil arrival and Mendelian randomisation is null, so the signal is weak evidence of a causal role.
reasons.claim: its rise reports in part cell arrival

verdicts.summary: A genetics-only hypothesis with no Mendelian randomisation support and no change in biopsies; I would not spend a first year on it.

reasons.text: Prediction is tiny (+0.036 in NK cells), biopsies show no change and there is no clinical drug; the card itself concedes it stays only to fill the list.
reasons.claim: Mendelian randomisation gives no support, and biopsies show no change

verdicts.summary: An approved factor B inhibitor is a convenient test, but the red safety light and the loss-of-function genetics point toward protection.

reasons.text: A CFB loss-of-function variant is associated with perianal Crohn's disease, implicating CFB activity in protection, though in a different phenotype from UC.
reasons.quote: pCD-associated rs4151651 in CFB is a loss-of-function mutation that impairs its cleavage, activation of alternative complement pathway, and pathogen phagocytosis thus implicating the alternative complement pathway and CFB in pCD aetiology.

reasons.text: Red safety light and complement's role in infection defence make chronic inhibition risky; an ex vivo test of the approved drug is still reasonable.
reasons.claim: long-term inhibition may reproduce that disease

verdicts.summary: A solid epithelial, intrinsic rise, but no functional or genetic evidence and no obvious drug route.

reasons.text: Reproducible and intrinsic, yet an intracellular enzyme with no extracellular part and a single list mention; it is a discovery bet, not an evidence-backed target.
reasons.claim: What is missing: any functional or genetic evidence

verdicts.summary: The only causal genetic signal, but the cell, the tissue direction and the drug route do not fit a first-year target.

reasons.text: Ubiquitous mitochondrial gene, one instrument, predicted cell differs from single-cell cell, and inflamed biopsies show a slight decrease; inhibition is unsupported in tissue.
reasons.claim: which does not support the inhibition hypothesis in tissue

verdicts.summary: A broadly expressed transcription factor with a cell mismatch and null Mendelian randomisation is not a first-year target.

reasons.text: Transcription factor, main source neutrophils and macrophages not the predicted dendritic cell, null genetics pointing the other way, and no clinical drug.
reasons.claim: a transcription factor is hard to drug

verdicts.summary: A strong marker with antibody tractability, but knockout mice show worse colitis, so blockade could harm the epithelium.

reasons.text: Chi3l1 knockout mice developed severe colitis but less colitis-associated cancer, so inhibition has opposing effects on injury and tumour.
reasons.quote: Here we demonstrate that CHI3L1 (aka Brp39) knockout (KO) mice treated with azoxymethane (AOM)/dextran sulphate sodium (DSS) developed severe colitis but lesser incidence of CAC as compared to that in wild-type (WT) mice.

reasons.text: The parallel fibroblast and organoid test is the right design, as it reads benefit and harm together.
reasons.claim: to see benefit and harm in one test

verdicts.summary: Same case as FIGNL1: a sequence-based prediction with no support from Mendelian randomisation or biopsies.

reasons.text: Tiny predicted effect, no change in biopsies, no genetic corroboration and no drug; confirming the variant effect on expression comes before any target claim.
reasons.claim: no Mendelian randomisation support and no change in biopsies

verdicts.summary: The best-supported choice: epithelial, intrinsic, reproducible, with knockdown benefit in mouse colitis; the cancer question needs care.

reasons.text: SerpinB5 knockdown relieved symptoms in a DSS mouse model of UC and reduced M1 macrophage polarisation.
reasons.quote: Meanwhile, SerpinB5 knockdown relieved symptoms of the mouse model of UC and repressed M1 macrophage polarization.

reasons.text: Safety light is green, but the tumour-suppressor annotation and recent, single-group mouse data justify organoid work before any antibody.
reasons.claim: its role in colitis-associated cancer is unsettled

verdicts.summary: A stromal, secreted target with a clean profile, but one expression paper and no mouse or genetic evidence.

reasons.text: Rises already in non-inflamed mucosa, and about 41% of the bulk rise is intrinsic; fibroblast silencing is a sensible first test, but the evidence base is thin.
reasons.claim: its literature is one expression paper

verdicts.summary: A real neutrophil-recruiting chemokine, but its rise is mostly neutrophil influx, and redundant CXCR2 ligands may blunt a single-ligand block.

reasons.text: Most of the bulk rise is composition; blocking one CXCR2 ligand among several may be compensated, and neutrophil clearance is needed for infection defence.
reasons.claim: blocking it would act on neutrophil recruitment rather than on a change of the tissue

verdicts.summary: Activin blockade has mouse colitis support and an approved ligand trap, but the gene is strongly constrained and the signal marks severity.

reasons.text: In DSS colitis, follistatin, an activin inhibitor, reduced inflammatory infiltrate and favoured epithelial repair.
reasons.quote: Importantly, in vivo administration of follistatin attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration during colitis.

reasons.text: LOEUF 0.17 and a non-replicating cell lineage argue for caution; sotatercept traps several activin and GDF ligands, not activin A alone.

verdicts.summary: Stromal and replicated across atlases, but only 28% of the rise is intrinsic, the in situ cell differs, and nothing functional exists.

reasons.text: BMP antagonist biology could cut either way in the mucosa; a single list paper, no mouse data, and the producing cell is unsettled.
reasons.claim: the producing cell is not settled

verdicts.summary: Mostly a local-inflammation signal with known safety events and mouse data that, against the card, show benefit of P-selectin blockade.

reasons.text: Anti-P-selectin antibody reduced leukocyte recruitment and colitis scores in DSS mice, so the animal data do support the pathway.
reasons.quote: Compared with control antibody-treated wild-type (WT) mice, WT mice treated with anti-P-selectin antibody and P-selectin(-/-) mice had significantly decreased leukocyte rolling and adhesion in colonic venules and reduced clinical and pathological colitis scores.

reasons.text: Not a tissue change, only partly intrinsic, no genetic support, and a class of adhesion-blocking drugs already tested in IBD; not a first-year pick.
reasons.claim: so it is a local-inflammation signal

verdicts.summary: A reproducible epithelial rise in regenerating crypts, but no functional evidence and a possible repair role.

reasons.text: Rises in crypt cells as a possible repair programme, so inhibition could slow healing; an orphan P450 with no paper beyond a list mention.
reasons.claim: What is missing: any functional or genetic evidence

objections.claim: in experimental colitis an anti-P-selectin antibody did not significantly improve colitis
objections.objection: A DSS colitis study found that anti-P-selectin antibody significantly reduced leukocyte recruitment and clinical and pathological colitis scores, so the claim of no improvement is contradicted.
objections.suggestion: State that anti-P-selectin antibody reduced colitis scores in DSS mice, or cite the study showing no improvement; do not present the animal result as negative.
objections.quote: Compared with control antibody-treated wild-type (WT) mice, WT mice treated with anti-P-selectin antibody and P-selectin(-/-) mice had significantly decreased leukocyte rolling and adhesion in colonic venules and reduced clinical and pathological colitis scores.

objections.objection: A p value of 0.484 is not support; the genetics light reads no causal effect.
objections.suggestion: Say plasma Mendelian randomisation is not significant.

objections.claim: an inhibitor is approved for ulcerative colitis and was never tried in UC or IBD
objections.objection: Self-contradictory: sotatercept is approved for pulmonary arterial hypertension, not UC, as the dossier states.
objections.suggestion: Write: an inhibitor is approved for pulmonary arterial hypertension and was never tried in UC or IBD.

objections.claim: so it predicts ustekinumab failure specifically
objections.objection: The same sentence says its baseline level separates ustekinumab and placebo non-responders alike, which means it is not specific to ustekinumab.
objections.suggestion: Say it marks severity, not ustekinumab failure specifically.

objections.objection: The card itself finds no functional study in either direction and a possible repair role; 'validated target' overstates a biomarker-only record.
objections.suggestion: Replace 'a validated target' with 'a supported biomarker, not yet a validated target'.

objections.claim: for CFB a loss-of-function variant implies its function drives the disease
objections.objection: The loss-of-function variant is associated with increased risk of perianal Crohn's disease, implying the function protects, as the CFB card says.
objections.suggestion: Write: for CFB a loss-of-function variant implies its function protects.
